subject: SLA baseline & monthly credit escalator — Orbit Analytics
messages:
From: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@orbitanalytics.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbitanalytics.com
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA discussion — baseline & credits

Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Orbit needs clarity on two items before procurement will approve: 1) the baseline uptime percentage you can commit to for our production cluster in us-east, and 2) how monthly service credits would scale if the baseline is missed in consecutive months. Our legal/compliance team wants a predictable escalator rather than an open-ended remedy.

Two asks from our side: can Redwood commit to a 99.95% uptime baseline for our dedicated pool, and can you provide an example monthly-credit escalator (e.g., 5% first breach month, 10% second consecutive month, capped at 25%)? Also we want to ensure there's a latency floor for P95 inference calls — better than 200ms for small chat requests.

Attached: uptime-metrics-aug-nov.csv (our observed patterns).

Warmly,
Luis Ortega
Head of Platform
Orbit Analytics

---
Attachment: uptime-metrics-aug-nov.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 10:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: SLA discussion — baseline & credits

Luis — thanks for the clear asks and the metrics file. Quick internal note: Marissa and Naomi on pricing & legal are looped so we can respond with an executable template.

High-level response: we can offer a 99.95% uptime baseline for a Dedicated pool in us-east, provided we align on maintenance windows and a few operational carve-outs (planned maint windows, mutually agreed disaster recovery tests). For consecutive-month remedies we typically use a graded monthly credit approach; below is an initial proposal we can take to procurement and legal: 

- Month 1 breach (99.95 -> observed): 5% of that month's committed fees
- Month 2 consecutive breach: 12% of that month's committed fees
- Month 3+ consecutive breaches: 20% monthly credits, capped at 30% total for a rolling 3-month period

We will propose a latency P95 target of 200ms for small chat paths when requests are routed to your dedicated pool and KV cache hit rates are typical. If your workload has large contexts or heavy embeddings, latency targets will need workload-specific adjustments.

I'll attach our SLA template with redlines marked for the escalator and latency floor. Marissa / Naomi — can you confirm if finance and legal are comfortable with the escalator caps above? Also need guidance on whether we can agree to a 99.95 baseline without an increased monthly commitment or if Orbit will accept a small uplift to the committed capacity pricing.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood_sla_template_v2.pdf (PDF, 76KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 09:18:00 -05:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Orbit escalator proposal — pricing and risk

Team — quick take before we send a formal counter:

1) Baseline: 99.95% for Dedicated is doable but let's require a 30-day notice for any changes to the configuration (to avoid transient noise counting as breach).
2) Escalator: Sean's numbers look inline with precedent but the cap needs a hard cap per-incident and per-quarter so Finance isn't on hook for runaway credits. Proposed edits: first breach 5%, second 10%, third+ 18%, quarterly cap 30% of committed fees.
3) Latency: P95 <200ms is aggressive but acceptable if we tie it to request size buckets and default to a fall-back 350ms for large contexts.
4) Charge uplift: recommend +7% on committed spend to support the 99.95 guarantee (we'll call it a reliability premium). Orbit can decide to accept or request alternate remedies (e.g., deeper credits instead of uplift).

Can Ben run quick numbers on expected credit exposure at 3%, 10%, 20% breach scenarios for their expected monthly burn? Naomi, flag any legal redlines (particularly force majeure/maintenance carveouts). I want this back to me by EOD Friday so we can send a clean proposal early next week.

Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redlines_orbit_v1.docx (DOCX, 22KB)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2025 14:07:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Orbit escalator proposal — pricing and risk

Marissa — ran a quick exposure model. Assumptions: committed monthly fee $120k; probability of breach month independently estimated low based on current telemetry but assume correlated failure for worst-case. Numbers below are monthly credit amounts (not cumulative):

- 5% credit -> $6,000
- 10% credit -> $12,000
- 18% credit -> $21,600
- With quarterly cap 30% -> $36,000 cap per quarter

If we add the +7% uplift to their committed spend, we increase monthly invoice to $128,400 which offsets expected exposure for a single breach month but reduces margin. Recommend selling uplift as optional — include both options in proposal: (A) no uplift + escalator credits with quarterly cap; (B) +7% uplift with reduced escalator (5%/8%/12% capped at 20%).

Ben
Director, Finance — Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@orbitanalytics.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Banerjee <aisha.b@orbitanalytics.com>, procurement@orbitanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2025 16:42:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: SLA baseline & monthly credit escalator — Orbit Analytics

Sean / Marissa — appreciate the proposal and the two options. Orbit procurement prefers Option A (no uplift) but needs a firm quarterly cap and a requirement that credits be applied as invoice adjustments (not cash refunds). Legal also asked for explicit maintenance window definition: we can accept up to 4 scheduled maintenance hours per calendar month if notified 72 hours in advance; anything beyond that must be negotiated.

On latency: we are willing to accept the size-bucket approach. Can Redwood draft concrete SLO language that defines small chat requests (<= 512 tokens) P95 <200ms measured at the ingress point to the dedicated pool, and a second tier for "large context" requests (512-2048 tokens) P95 <350ms? We will take the formal SLA with those SLOs and the Option A escalator (5% / 12% / 20% capping quarterly at 30%) to Procurement next week, but we want the redlined SLA back for signature.

Two small items: please include a clause about model fallback (if our pinned model is unavailable, Redwood must automatically route to a compatible variant and log the fallback event) and add a simple reporting cadence (monthly SLA summary + incident write-ups when crediting).

Thanks,
Luis
Head of Platform — Orbit Analytics

---
Notes: procurement@orbitanalytics.com confirmed via separate thread they will expect invoice crediting. Orbit referenced prior months in uptime-metrics-aug-nov.csv showing two short outages in September tied to maintenance miscoordination.
